title: Bounce-Back Candidates
brief: Which players had a down season from injury, role or a shooting or steals slump and could return to their earlier level? It must explain why one bad season should not set the price and which bounce-backs depend on unstable stats.
summary: One bad season should not set a player's price. The experts say injuries, role changes and shooting slumps often reverse, and drafters fear returning players too much. In our 200 USD auction, the best buys are players the market dropped far below their earlier level, like Jalen Williams, Paul George and Dyson Daniels. Pay for the stats that are stable, and treat a recovery in FG% or three-point shooting as upside, not as part of the price.

sections.heading: Why one season should not set the price

paragraphs.text: The experts agree on the basic rule. One bad season does not make a player bad. Do not value a player on a single season, and do not let one year flip a long-term story such as "injury prone" or "reliable". In our auction, that means you should not anchor on last season's line when you set your maximum bid.

Injuries cause the biggest overreaction. Drafters are too scared of players whose injuries cost them last season, so you can be more confident than their ADPs suggest. Jalen Williams is the clearest case. Experts say the market dropped him too far after an injury-hit year, and they see him as a round three to four player. Paul George is another. Experts agree he is underpriced and see a top 40 per-game player with top 30 upside.

The same rule cuts both ways. Coby White has now had a fourth calf strain in 12 months. That is a long pattern, not one bad year, so experts moved him from the 60s to 70s into the 90s. Do not treat a repeated injury as bad luck. The bounce-back case is strongest when a player was reliable for years and then had one bad season.

Bounce-back candidates come from three sources: role changes, injuries and shooting slumps. Each one needs a different check in the first weeks, so know which kind of bounce-back you are buying before you bid.

Role. Zach LaVine finished 115th last season in a spot-up role, and his case rests on getting the ball back in his hands. Jalen Green needs to keep the point guard job and play 30 or more minutes. Coby White needs 30-plus minutes as the starting point guard. Domantas Sabonis needs his minutes to climb back toward 33 and his assists toward 6 with Simmons starting next to him. If the role does not show up, the bounce-back does not happen.

Injury. Jayson Tatum is coming back from an Achilles injury, and his FG% and rim finishing are expected to recover. Jalen Williams needs his hamstring to hold up. Jakob Poeltl's down year is blamed on his back. Christian Braun needs his 3P% and finishing to come back after an ankle injury. For each of them, check games played and minutes before you judge the box score.

Usage. One note says lower efficiency can bounce back when a player's usage is reduced. Derrick White shot 39.4% last season and now plays behind Tatum and George. Lower usage could help his FG%, but it could also push his minutes under 34. Trae Young's 42% FG% sits next to an open question about how much usage he keeps next to Davis and Dybantsa.

FT% drops are the safest bet. Several players had big free throw drops for no clear reason, and the notes treat that as a pattern that likely reverts. John Collins, Jalen Green and Coby White all fell below their usual FT% last season. Count on most of that coming back.

Steals move in both directions. Do not pay for a career-high steal rate. A player whose steals dropped can bounce back, though, because elite skills like steals tend to snap back after a down year. Dyson Daniels is the key case. He is a steals specialist, and his price should assume his steals climb back toward 2 per game. If they stay low after the first weeks, his value falls a lot.

FG% and three-point slumps are less certain. The notes say these slumps produce bounce-back candidates, but they only call the FT% drop a likely reversion. So do not pay up front for a recovery in FG% or 3P%. That applies to Daniels from three (18% last season), Tari Eason (41.6% FG after a poor three-point stretch), Derrick White, Paul George (about 44% FG) and Bam Adebayo. Price these players on their counting stats and treat better shooting as upside.

Punt builds lower the risk. Derrick White, Bam Adebayo, Trae Young, Myles Turner and Jalen Green all fit punt FG% builds. If you are punting FG%, an FG% recovery that never comes costs you nothing, and you still get their threes, assists, rebounds or blocks.

The experts split on three bigger names. On Ivica Zubac, one side sees a bounce-back, but Josh doubts he returns to top 30 form, and the group caps him at about 14 USD, rank 60 to 75. On Myles Turner, one expert calls him a strong bounce-back with top 60 upside, while the markets price him near nothing. On Christian Braun, Moore predicts a bounce-back, while others only expect him to finish better than outside the top 200. The markets also split on Trae Young. Yahoo still values him highly, but ESPN values him at only 11 USD and the experts call him a bust at his Yahoo rank of 18. In each case, bid at the cautious side's price. You then get the optimist's upside for free.

sections.heading: Auction and waiver plan for our league

paragraphs.text: Early in the auction, the bounce-backs worth real money are Tatum, Jalen Williams, Sabonis and Adebayo. Tatum is a fair buy in the high 40s to mid 50s USD and fits punt TO best. Williams is a good buy at 20 to 25 USD, but not at 29 USD. Sabonis is fine in the low 30s USD, not at 40 USD. Adebayo is worth up to about 27 USD. Check the Yahoo Q tags on Adebayo (groin) and Sabonis before you bid.

Most of the value comes in the middle rounds. Paul George at 10 to 15 USD is the best price gap (Josh would go to 20 USD). Daniels is a buy under 20 USD. Target Derrick White in the 13 to 25 USD range. Bid 10 to 14 USD on Zubac, 5 to 10 USD on Coby White and about 5 to 12 USD on LaVine. Avoid Trae Young unless his price fits a player around pick 26.

At the end of the draft, take bounce-back flyers for 1 to 5 USD: Turner, Collins, Green, Poeltl, Cameron Johnson, Eason and Braun. Aaron Nesmith sits just outside our 144 players, so put him on your waiver watch list unless you need a 1 USD punt AST pick. Waivers run daily on FAB with up to 6 adds a week, so cut a flyer quickly if his minutes or his key stat do not come back in the first weeks.

Check playoff schedules before you pay. Boston (Tatum, George, Derrick White) has 16 back-to-backs, with three in our playoff weeks, so watch who sits. Miami and Houston get only 10 playoff games. Indiana plays 3, 4 and 3 games in weeks 19 to 21. Phoenix's 4-4-4 schedule adds value to Green.
